turns.prompt_text: I'm going to try to print TPU through my Bambu A1
turns.response_html:
Printing TPU on the A1 is entirely doable, but it requires a very different approach than rigid plastics.

First and most importantly: do not feed standard flexible TPU (like 95A or 85A) through the AMS Lite.

Because TPU is so flexible, the AMS Lite's gears will try to push it through the long PTFE tubes, causing the filament to buckle and jam inside the hub. You will have to take the unit apart to clear it. You must mount the spool on the external holder and feed it directly into the toolhead. (The only exception is Bambu's recently released 68D "TPU for AMS," which is stiff enough to survive the tubes).

Here is how to set up the A1 for a successful flexible print:

Hardware & Preparation

  • The Hotend: Swap in one of your 0.4mm or 0.6mm hardened steel hotends if it isn't mounted already. Stay far away from 0.2mm nozzles when printing TPU, as the backpressure will cause them to clog almost immediately. It is highly recommended to do a cold pull before loading the TPU to clear out any old plastic.
  • Dry the Filament: TPU absorbs moisture out of the air incredibly fast. Even if it is fresh out of a factory-sealed vacuum bag, it almost always needs to be dried (70°C for ~8 hours). If you skip this, the moisture boils in the nozzle, resulting in severe stringing, popping noises, and weak layer adhesion.
  • The Build Plate: Stick to the Textured PEI plate. TPU adheres so aggressively to smooth plates that it can actually rip the coating off when you try to remove the print.

Slicer Settings & Physics

When transitioning from the rigid PLA and PETG you used for your Langstroth hive frames to a flexible material, the physical mechanics of the printer become a much bigger factor.

  • Tame the Wobble: The A1 is a "bed slinger"—it moves the entire build plate back and forth on the Y-axis. Because TPU is flexible, tall or skinny prints will act like a metronome and wobble violently as the print gets higher. You will need to add more physical supports than usual to brace the model, or the upper layers will fail.
  • Speed: You have to print agonizingly slow. Start with Bambu Studio's "Generic TPU" profile, but if you hear the extruder clicking or see under-extrusion, drop the Max Volumetric Speed setting even lower.

Post-Print Removal

When the print finishes, do not pull it straight off the bed. Flex the PEI plate slightly, spray some isopropyl alcohol at the base of the part, and let it wick underneath. The alcohol temporarily breaks the bond, allowing the TPU to peel off effortlessly without stretching or tearing your new part.
